title: Clyde McCoy and the Chicago walkathon
summary: He appeared with Clyde McCoy and performed at a Coliseum walkathon, describing contestants and songs sung.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Lee, at one time or other, didn't you have Clyde McCoy play with you?
Yes, I appeared with Clyde McCoy in quite a number of places. Some of them were in ballrooms and some of them were in nightclubs, supper clubs.
Lee, didn't you also work in some walkathons in Chicago?

Yes, I appeared at the Coliseum there to over 75,000. I took a show from the Club Vista nightclub at 47th and Cottage Grove where I was appearing. And was very well received and they got a huge kick out of my coon shouting.
Tell about how the people drug themselves.

Oh, and I was appearing there and the people, actually it was a walkathon. And I got a kick out of the way they were dragging one another around either by the hair or the head or by their heels or the arms or any way they could drag them around. One would be asleep and the other would be dragging him around or he'd be out from desolation.
Didn't the manager of the Coliseum, the owner, call up your manager at the Club Vista at the time?

Yes, when I got back to the Club Vista, well they had a various number of calls and the manager had also called from the walkathon and told my boss what a wonderful show that I put on and how I was received.
What were some of the songs you sang around then? What, Coconut Island or were some of those around, was that popular around that time?
Well, at that show that night I sang I Can't Dance and was popular and on the Coconut Island and Stay Away from Dixieland.
